behaviors: Read demand, ready, reset, forwarding, source loop and visibility branches. Exact topic demand drives one shared conversation receiver; last release closes it, a replacement gets a fresh generation, and unknown/hidden/remote rows fail closed. Only admitted visible local rows publish ready or conversation deltas.

Broker accepts private Delivery immediately before publication: ready activates only its own current generation; stale ready/delta cannot activate or disclose a replacement. Existing broker tests prove stale deltas/hidden or unknown rows are dropped; added stale-ready test proves the prior generation cannot open the new barrier.

Typed source preserves the ConversationDelta data model; real embedded-engine integration compares full serialized source delta and forwarded value. There is no mutation replay. Broadcast lag invalidates buffered fragments and requires a new ready before fresh data.
intentionalChanges: Full standalone and native now own the embedded Rust engine, so a demand-owned typed broadcast receiver replaces the Go SSE client/reconnect/backoff loop. serve::plan_serve only allows a borrowed external daemon in explicit hub-only mode; its read-only event link is not represented as the full brain conversation producer.

Data is serialized from the canonical typed delta, not forwarded as byte-identical raw JSON. Unknown extra wire fields and original JSON whitespace are not claimed preserved. Ready is broker-committed instead of callback delivery under a Go pointer/channel barrier.

The in-process producer has no independent bus reconnection. Broker subscriber disconnects release demand; new subscriber demand recreates the receiver/ready contract. Producer closure is an owned runtime failure rather than an indefinitely retrying external HTTP connection.
